Before there was a Hindu and a Zoroastrian, there was one people on the Eurasian steppe who sang to the same god.
When the Indo-Iranians split one branch flowing south into the Saptasindhu, the other west into the Iranian plateau they took the same hymns with them. In India, the warrior-god became indr, the slayer of vritr. In Iran, he became (Verethragna), later Bahram (the smasher of obstruction).
Vritra-han becomes Verethra-gna. Same name. Same god. Different language.
